intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, combining gentle flow yoga with breathtaking natural views to start your day mindfully.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon at the iconic Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful stretches of golden sand. Take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson with a local instructor, then relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset from the shore or a nearby beachfront spot.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Attend several drop-in yoga and meditation classes at The Yoga Barn, one of Bali's most celebrated wellness centers. With a wide variety of styles including Hatha, Vinyasa, and Yin, this is a perfect ongoing experience across your 13-day stay to deepen your practice in a serene jungle setting.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Escape to the pristine, calm waters of Nusa Dua, known for its white sandy beaches and turquoise sea. Ideal for swimming and snorkeling, this upscale beach area offers a more relaxed and uncrowded experience. Rent a sun lounger and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere away from the busier tourist spots.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Ubud Market Tour
experiences.description: Start with an early morning guided tour of the vibrant Ubud Traditional Market to discover exotic local spices, fruits, and ingredients. Then head to a family-run cooking school to learn how to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like Nasi Goreng, Satay, and Lawar. A delicious cultural immersion that feeds both body and soul.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency at the airport for a fair rate, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer or take a Bluebird taxi to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in to Campuhan Ridge Ubud Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a slow walk along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to soak in the lush green hillside views and decompress after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Jalan Raya Campuhan strip on foot. Visit a local warung (small family-run eatery) for your first taste of authentic Balinese food. Head to bed early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip — arrival at 13:00
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside warung en route to Ubud — try nasi campur (mixed rice) for around IDR 20,000–35,000 (~$1.50–$2.50)
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka or a local warung near Campuhan Ridge — budget IDR 30,000–50,000 (~$2–$4) for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: Keep day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Avoid booking tours or activities on arrival day. Confirm your accommodation check-in time in advance. Bring small IDR bills for tipping and local transport.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00 AM) and take the Campuhan Ridge Walk at sunrise — one of Ubud's most beautiful and completely free experiences. The 2 km trail winds through rice fields and jungle with panoramic views. Return to the hotel for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in central Ubud (entry ~IDR 80,000 / ~$5). Stroll through the ancient temple complex and dense jungle, observing Balinese long-tailed macaques. Afterward, browse the Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni) for local crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs — practice your bargaining skills.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Jalan Hanoman and Jalan Dewi Sita for evening atmosphere. Catch a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Arma Open Stage (tickets ~IDR 100,000–150,000 / ~$7–$10). A must-see cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try a local nasi goreng or bubur ayam (rice porridge) for IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka near the Monkey Forest or Warung Teges — nasi campur or babi guling for IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Warung Biah Biah on Jalan Goutama — authentic Balinese cuisine at budget prices, mains around IDR 40,000–60,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the ridge walk. Bring a light rain jacket — July is generally dry but afternoon showers are possible. Wear a sarong (or rent one at the entrance) to enter the Monkey Forest temple areas.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning yoga class at one of Ubud's affordable yoga studios. Yoga Barn (Jalan Hanoman) offers drop-in classes from IDR 130,000–180,000 (~$8–$12). Choose a 7:00 or 8:00 AM session — options include Hatha, Vinyasa, or Yin. Return to the hotel to freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pura Taman Saraswati (Ubud Water Palace) — free to view from outside, small donation if entering. Then explore Blanco Renaissance Museum (IDR 80,000) or simply wander Ubud's cultural streets. Head to the Ubud Traditional Market in the afternoon when it's less crowded.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost meditation or sound healing session — many studios in Ubud offer community evening events. Check Yoga Barn's schedule. Wind down with herbal tea at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Kafe (Jalan Hanoman) — healthy smoothie bowls and toast from IDR 45,000–70,000, popular with the yoga crowd
meals.lunch: Warung Sopa (vegetarian-friendly) on Jalan Sugriwa — full meal for IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Warung Mendez or Warung Kelapa near Campuhan — local Balinese dishes for IDR 35,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes in advance online or arrive 15 minutes early — popular morning sessions fill up quickly. Bring your own mat if you have one to avoid rental fees (~IDR 20,000 extra). Stay hydrated in the warm weather.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter (scooter rental ~IDR 70,000–100,000/day) and cycle through the Tegallalang Rice Terraces (20 min north of Ubud). Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat crowds and enjoy the cool morning light over the UNESCO-listed stepped paddies. Entry fee ~IDR 15,000–20,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to Tirta Empul Temple (entry ~IDR 50,000) — a sacred Hindu water temple where locals and visitors participate in a traditional purification ritual in natural spring pools. Dress respectfully (sarong provided). Explore the temple grounds and observe ceremonies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud by scooter. Visit Jalan Raya Ubud for window shopping and people-watching. Enjoy a relaxed evening near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel or grab a banana pancake from a local street stall near Campuhan (~IDR 15,000–25,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near Tegallalang or Tirta Empul — nasi goreng or mie goreng for IDR 25,000–40,000 at a roadside warung
meals.dinner: Tutmak Café on Jalan Dewi Sita — cozy budget-friendly café with Indonesian and Western options, mains IDR 45,000–75,000

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have an international driving permit and wear a helmet at all times. The road to Tegallalang can be narrow — drive cautiously. Bring cash as many roadside stalls don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or stretching session on your own — use the hotel grounds or return to Campuhan Ridge Walk for a mindful walk and gentle movement in nature. Practice pranayama breathing exercises as the sun rises over the jungle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a shared shuttle or hire a driver (~IDR 200,000–300,000 for a half-day) to visit Pura Besakih — Bali's most important and largest temple complex, known as the 'Mother Temple,' set dramatically on the slopes of Mount Agung. Entry ~IDR 60,000. Alternatively, visit the closer Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) temple, just 4 km from Ubud (entry ~IDR 50,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Treat yourself to a budget Balinese massage — many spas along Jalan Hanoman offer 1-hour traditional massages for IDR 80,000–120,000 (~$5–$8). Perfect post-yoga recovery.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Wayan on Jalan Monkey Forest — full breakfast for IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Besakih or Goa Gajah — simple local meal for IDR 25,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Naughty Nuri's Warung (Jalan Raya Sanggingan) — famous ribs and Indonesian dishes, budget IDR 60,000–90,000 for a filling meal

day_by_day.notes: Besakih Temple requires a guide (IDR 100,000–150,000) — negotiate firmly and agree on the price before starting. A sarong is mandatory. If visiting Goa Gajah, bring a swimsuit as there are bathing pools. Both sites are best visited in the morning before midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the beaches of Seminyak or Canggu — arrange a shared shuttle from Ubud (IDR 60,000–80,000 one way via Kura-Kura Bus or Perama shuttle). Arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM. Spend the morning on Batu Bolong Beach (Canggu) — a laid-back surf beach with a great vibe and free beach access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Canggu's beach strip. Explore Echo Beach or Pererenan Beach — both free and less crowded than Kuta. Dip your toes in the Indian Ocean and watch local surfers. Browse the Canggu street art and boutique scene.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the famous Bali sunset from the beach (around 6:00–6:30 PM in July). Head to a beachside warung for a sundowner coconut or Bintang beer (~IDR 25,000–40,000). Take the evening shuttle back to Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Eat before leaving Ubud — hotel breakfast or grab takeaway from a local café
meals.lunch: Old Man's Beach Bar or a warung on Batu Bolong Beach — grilled fish, nasi campur for IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Eat dinner in Canggu before the return shuttle, or pick up a simple warung meal back in Ubud for IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the shuttle the day before from your hotel or a local travel agent on Jalan Raya Ubud. Confirm the return shuttle time in advance — last shuttles typically depart around 5:00–6:00 PM. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. July is peak season so beaches can be busy.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, do a gentle self-guided yoga practice, or enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend the morning journaling or reading in a café near Campuhan Ridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-known Penestanan village, just a short walk from Campuhan — a quiet artists' village with rice paddies, studios, and galleries. Visit local painters' workshops (many are free to browse). Walk the scenic path between Penestanan and Sayan village.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or donation-based community event in Ubud — check noticeboards at Yoga Barn or Bali Spirit for workshops, kirtan (devotional singing), or cultural evenings. Many are free or pay-what-you-can.

meals.breakfast: Lazy breakfast at a café — try Seniman Coffee Studio (Jalan Sri Wedari) for excellent local Balinese coffee and light bites, budget IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Warung in Penestanan village — extremely local and cheap, full meal for IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Warung Bernadette (Jalan Raya Campuhan) — simple, home-cooked Balinese food close to the hotel, IDR 30,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to do laundry (laundry services in Ubud cost ~IDR 15,000–20,000 per kg), restock supplies, and plan the second half of the trip. Check your budget and adjust spending if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga class at Yoga Barn (7:00 AM session). Try a different style — Kundalini, Aerial, or Restorative yoga for variety. After class, take a refreshing dip in Yoga Barn's natural pool (included with class ticket).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pura Gunung Kawi — an ancient 11th-century temple and royal tomb complex carved into cliff faces in the Pakerisan River gorge (~IDR 50,000 entry, 15 km north of Ubud). Descend 315 steps to the riverside — breathtaking and uncrowded compared to Besakih. Combine with a stop at Tirta Empul if you missed it on Day 4.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Explore the Ubud night food stalls near the Ubud Palace — local satay, corn on the cob, and fresh fruit for very cheap. Watch the evening activity around the palace grounds.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie or açaí bowl at Kafe (Jalan Hanoman) — IDR 50,000–75,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Gunung Kawi — simple nasi campur for IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Night market stalls near Ubud Palace — satay skewers, martabak (stuffed pancake), fresh coconut for IDR 20,000–40,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Gunung Kawi requires a sarong — available to borrow at the entrance. The steps are steep; wear good footwear. The site is most peaceful on weekday mornings. Combine with Tirta Empul (nearby) to make the most of the trip north.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day beach excursion to the Bukit Peninsula (south Bali) — arrange a driver or shared shuttle to Padang Padang Beach or Bingin Beach (~IDR 200,000–300,000 for a return private driver, or IDR 100,000–150,000 shared). Arrive early to claim a good spot. Padang Padang is a stunning cove (entry IDR 10,000) famous for its turquoise water and cliff setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Padang Padang to Bingin Beach (15–20 min walk) — a dramatic cliff-backed beach popular with surfers. Rent a surfboard for IDR 50,000–80,000/hour if interested. Swim, snorkel, or simply sunbathe. The water is warm and clear in July.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Bukit cliffs — Uluwatu Temple (entry IDR 50,000) offers one of Bali's most iconic sunset views. Catch the Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu at 6:00 PM (tickets IDR 100,000–150,000) — set dramatically on the cliff edge above the ocean. Return to Ubud by 9:00–10:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Ubud — hotel or quick warung breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach warung at Bingin or Padang Padang — grilled fish, nasi goreng, fresh coconut for IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Warung near Uluwatu before heading back, or eat in Ubud on return — budget IDR 35,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: The Kecak Dance at Uluwatu is one of Bali's top experiences — book tickets on arrival at the temple (no advance booking needed, but arrive 30 min early for good seats). Bring a sarong for temple entry. The road to Bukit is winding — confirm your driver knows the route.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation or breathwork session — either self-guided on Campuhan Ridge or join a community class at Yoga Barn or The Radiantly Alive studio. Spend the rest of the morning at leisure — read, journal, or nap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bali's Botanical Garden (Kebun Raya Bali) in Bedugul (~1.5 hrs from Ubud by scooter or shared transport, entry ~IDR 40,000). Explore 157 hectares of highland gardens with over 2,000 plant species. Combine with a stop at Pura Ulun Danu Bratan — the iconic water temple floating on Lake Bratan (entry ~IDR 75,000). Stunning mountain and lake scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening near the hotel — take a stroll along the ridge at dusk and watch fireflies emerge over the jungle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local warung near Campuhan — nasi goreng or fruit plate for IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Bedugul market — local Balinese food at very low prices (IDR 20,000–35,000), try fresh strawberries sold by the roadside
meals.dinner: Warung Biah Biah or Warung Bernadette near Campuhan — home-cooked dinner for IDR 35,000–55,000

day_by_day.notes: Bedugul is at higher elevation (~1,200 m) — bring a light jacket as it can feel cool, especially in the morning. The lake temple is especially beautiful in the early afternoon light. If using a scooter, the road north from Ubud is scenic but has some steep sections.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike up Mount Batur (active volcano, 1,717 m). This requires a very early start — depart Ubud at 2:00–2:30 AM by pre-arranged driver (IDR 200,000–300,000 return). Summit hike takes 2 hours with a local guide (mandatory, ~IDR 350,000–450,000 per person including guide). Reach the summit by 5:30 AM for a breathtaking sunrise above the clouds and Lake Batur below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend by 9:00–10:00 AM. Stop at a hot spring near Lake Batur (Toya Devasya or local hot springs, IDR 50,000–150,000 entry) to soak tired muscles. Return to Ubud by early afternoon and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Very relaxed evening — light stretching or gentle yoga to recover. Early dinner and early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on the volcano summit — guides typically bring basic eggs cooked in volcanic steam and instant noodles (included or IDR 20,000–30,000 extra)
meals.lunch: Warung near Lake Batur or Kintamani — nasi campur for IDR 25,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Simple warung meal near the hotel — keep it light (soup, steamed rice, vegetables) for IDR 30,000–45,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the Mount Batur hike through your hotel or a local Ubud trekking agency the day before. Wear warm layers for the summit (temperature drops significantly at night). Bring a headlamp, water, and snacks. The hike is moderately challenging but suitable for reasonably fit travelers. This is a highlight of any Bali trip — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the Batur hike. Sleep in, do gentle stretching, and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Ubud Organic Market (held Saturday mornings at Jalan Raya Ubud) if the timing aligns — browse local produce, organic snacks, and handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach day — take a shuttle to Sanur Beach on Bali's calmer east coast (IDR 60,000–80,000 one way via shuttle). Sanur has a peaceful, reef-protected lagoon — ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Walk the 4 km beachside promenade. Rent a snorkel set for IDR 30,000–50,000 and explore the shallow reef.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Sanur sunset from the beach — the east-facing coast has beautiful morning light but also lovely evening colors. Return to Ubud by shuttle. Pack bags for departure tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Organic market snacks or café breakfast near Jalan Raya Ubud — fresh juices, smoothies, local pastries for IDR 35,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Warung at Sanur beachfront — grilled seafood, nasi goreng for IDR 40,000–65,000
meals.dinner: Final dinner in Ubud — revisit a favorite warung or try Locavore To Go (affordable takeaway version of Ubud's famous farm-to-table restaurant) — IDR 60,000–90,000

day_by_day.notes: Sanur is a great alternative to the busier Kuta or Seminyak — calmer water, less crowd, more local feel. The beach promenade is flat and easy to walk. Check shuttle return times carefully for your last evening in Ubud.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last Campuhan Ridge Walk at sunrise. Take your time to absorb the beauty of Ubud's landscape. Return to the hotel, pack remaining items, and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, explore any last spots in Ubud — pick up final souvenirs at the Ubud Art Market, grab a fresh coconut, or enjoy a final coffee at Seniman Coffee. Arrange airport transfer (pre-book through hotel or use Grab app, budget IDR 150,000–250,000 to Ngurah Rai Airport, approximately 1.5–2 hrs).
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive plus check-in. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Final Balinese breakfast at the hotel or a nearby warung — nasi goreng, fresh fruit, Bali coffee for IDR 25,000–45,000
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Ubud before departure — grab a takeaway wrap or smoothie for IDR 30,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and airport transfer the night before. Leave a small tip for hotel staff if you were happy with the service (IDR 50,000–100,000 is appreciated). Keep IDR 200,000–300,000 in cash for airport tax, tips, and last-minute purchases. Bali departure tax is usually included in the ticket but confirm with your airline.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay (~1.5 hrs). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to soak in the rolling green hills and river valley views
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Ubud town center on foot — browse Jalan Raya Ubud, visit a local art shop, and settle into the Bali vibe

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at the hotel or a warung near the property upon arrival
meals.dinner: Locavore To Go or Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka for an authentic Balinese first dinner experience (~IDR 80,000–150,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Hydrate well — Bali humidity can be intense. Exchange currency at a reputable money changer in Ubud rather than the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise yoga class at the Yoga Barn in Ubud (~7:00–9:00 AM) — one of Bali's most celebrated yoga studios set amid lush jungle surroundings
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud, then explore the Ubud Art Market and Palace (Puri Saren Agung) nearby
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Ubud Palace or Pura Dalem Ubud (~6:00–7:30 PM)

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Kafe Ubud for smoothie bowls and eggs (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Sopa for healthy Balinese vegetarian cuisine (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Bridges Bali restaurant overlooking the Campuhan River gorge (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga class in advance via The Yoga Barn website. Kecak performances are weather-dependent — check ahead. Wear closed shoes or sandals you don't mind getting dirty at the Monkey Forest.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and pranayama session at Radiantly Alive yoga studio, followed by a walk through the Campuhan Ridge trail at golden hour
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Tegallalang Rice Terraces (~20 min from Ubud) — walk the terraced paddies, take photos, and interact with local farmers. Visit a nearby coffee plantation for a Luwak coffee tasting
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud and explore the night market scene around Jalan Dewi Sita

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio for specialty coffee and avocado toast (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Warung at Tegallalang Rice Terraces — simple nasi campur with a view (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Ubud for a refined Indonesian tasting menu — a mid-range splurge (~IDR 300,000–500,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tegallalang has a small entry fee (~IDR 15,000). Wear sunscreen and a hat. Luwak coffee tasting is free if you purchase a cup (~IDR 50,000–80,000).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tirta Empul Temple (~30 min from Ubud) for a spiritual purification ritual in the sacred spring pools — a deeply authentic Balinese experience
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Kanto Lampo Waterfall or Tegenungan Waterfall for a refreshing swim and nature walk
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing spa evening — book a traditional Balinese massage and flower bath at a local spa in Ubud

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Kafe at Penestanan for fresh juices and granola
meals.lunch: Naughty Nuri's Warung for BBQ ribs and cold Bintang (~IDR 100,000–180,000)
meals.dinner: Hujan Locale for modern Indonesian cuisine with local ingredients (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly at Tirta Empul — a sarong and sash are required and available for rent at the temple entrance (~IDR 15,000). Arrive early to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day begins — take a 1.5-hour transfer to Seminyak or Canggu beach. Arrive early to claim a good spot and enjoy a morning yoga stretch on the sand
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim, sunbathe, and rent a surfboard for a beginner lesson on the gentle Canggu waves (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for 1-hour lesson)
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Bali sunset from a beach club — Finns Beach Club (Canggu) or La Plancha (Seminyak) for a cocktail and sunset view

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at hotel before departure or stop at a café en route
meals.lunch: Warung Dandelion or local warungs in Canggu for nasi goreng or fresh seafood (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Petitenget restaurant in Seminyak for upscale Indonesian fare with a beachside atmosphere (~IDR 200,000–350,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book a private driver for the day (~IDR 400,000–600,000) for flexibility. Bring reef-safe sunscreen. July is dry season so beach conditions should be excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise yoga session on the beach or at a local studio in Canggu (e.g., The Practice or Samadi Bali)
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seminyak's boutique shopping strip along Jalan Oberoi — pick up local fashion, jewelry, and handmade goods. Visit Ku De Ta beach for an afternoon swim
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Seminyak's restaurant row and enjoy a relaxed dinner before heading back to Ubud

meals.breakfast: Betelnut Café in Seminyak for healthy bowls and fresh juices (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Sisterfields café in Seminyak for brunch-style plates (~IDR 100,000–160,000)
meals.dinner: Mama San for creative Asian cuisine in Seminyak (~IDR 150,000–250,000) before transfer back to Ubud

day_by_day.notes: Shopping in Seminyak is great for mid-range finds. Always bargain politely at local boutiques. Arrange return transfer to Ubud by 8–9 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day — slow morning at the hotel, journaling, or a gentle walk along the Campuhan Ridge at your own pace
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Balinese cooking class in Ubud (e.g., Paon Bali or Casa Luna Cooking School) — visit a local market, then cook 4–5 traditional dishes
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the meal you cooked! Afterward, join a sound healing or cacao ceremony session at The Yoga Barn

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Pomegranate for a light healthy start
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cooking class (~IDR 350,000–500,000 total for the class)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Warung Teges or a simple local warung near the hotel (~IDR 50,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically run 9 AM–1 PM or 4–8 PM. Book at least 2 days in advance. This is a great mid-trip reset day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Batur — depart by 2:00 AM for a guided sunrise trek to the volcano summit (1,717m). Reach the top by sunrise (~5:30 AM) for breathtaking panoramic views
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and stop at Lake Batur for a relaxing soak in natural hot springs. Drive back to Ubud by early afternoon
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover at the hotel. Optional: gentle yin yoga class at The Yoga Barn in the evening

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast provided by the trek guide at the summit (usually eggs cooked in volcanic steam)
meals.lunch: Warung near Lake Batur for local Balinese food (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Room service or a very light meal at a nearby warung — you'll be tired! (~IDR 50,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified guide through your hotel or a reputable agency (~IDR 300,000–500,000 per person including guide and transport). Bring warm layers — it's cold at the summit. The trek is moderately challenging but manageable for most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in, then enjoy a Balinese boreh body scrub and massage at a spa in Ubud (e.g., COMO Shambhala or Karsa Spa)
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum celebrating Ubud's most famous foreign artist, then walk through the Penestanan artist village to browse local galleries
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong dance performance at Puri Saren Ubud Palace (~IDR 100,000 per person)

meals.breakfast: Lazy Cat Café for smoothies and eggs benedict (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Clear Café Ubud for organic, health-conscious fare (~IDR 80,000–140,000)
meals.dinner: Barbecue and tapas at Merah Putih Ubud or a riverside warung (~IDR 120,000–200,000)

day_by_day.notes: Spa treatments should be booked in advance. Blanco Museum entrance fee is ~IDR 50,000. Dance performances usually begin at 7:30 PM — arrive 15 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Nusa Dua or Pandawa Beach — take a 1.5-hour transfer south. Pandawa Beach is quieter and more scenic with dramatic limestone cliffs
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or stand-up paddleboarding at Pandawa Beach (~IDR 100,000–200,000 for equipment rental). Relax on the white sand
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Uluwatu Temple perched on a 70m cliff for sunset views and a Kecak Fire Dance performance

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled seafood at a beachside warung at Pandawa (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.dinner: Single Fin restaurant at Uluwatu for burgers and cocktails with ocean views (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong at Uluwatu Temple — required and available at the entrance. Watch out for monkeys stealing sunglasses and phones. Book return driver for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on the Campuhan Ridge — do a self-guided practice or join a guided outdoor yoga session offered by some local instructors
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) and Yeh Pulu archaeological site — ancient Hindu and Buddhist carvings dating back to the 9th century
day_by_day.evening: Take a batik or silver jewelry-making workshop in Ubud for a hands-on cultural experience

meals.breakfast: Tutmak Café for Indonesian-style breakfast with rice porridge (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka 2 for babi guling (suckling pig) — a Balinese classic (~IDR 80,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Indus Restaurant overlooking the Campuhan River for Indonesian and international fusion (~IDR 150,000–250,000)

day_by_day.notes: Goa Gajah entrance fee is ~IDR 50,000. Sarong required. Silver jewelry workshops typically cost IDR 200,000–400,000 and last 2–3 hours — book through your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach excursion — head to Balangan Beach or Bingin Beach in Uluwatu for a more secluded, surfer-vibe experience with dramatic cliff scenery
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and relax, then explore the cliff-top cafés and surf shops. Optional: book a final surf lesson on the gentle reef break
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud for a farewell dinner and a reflective walk along the Campuhan Ridge at dusk

meals.breakfast: Quick healthy breakfast before departure — Kafe Ubud or hotel
meals.lunch: Cashew Tree café at Bingin Beach for smoothie bowls and wraps with a cliff view (~IDR 80,000–140,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Locavore, Ubud's celebrated farm-to-table restaurant — book well in advance (~IDR 400,000–700,000 for tasting menu)

day_by_day.notes: Balangan and Bingin beaches require a short steep walk down — wear appropriate footwear. Locavore is one of Asia's top restaurants — reservations are essential and should be made weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the Campuhan Ridge — take in the misty green hills one last time. Pack and check out of the hotel
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Ubud Art Market — pick up batik fabrics, wood carvings, and Balinese jewelry. Grab a final coffee at Seniman Coffee Studio
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport for departure. Reflect on an incredible 13-day Bali journey

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Pomegranate for a light final morning meal
meals.lunch: Warung Bernadette or a simple local warung for a casual last Balinese lunch (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the hotel before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer and check-in. Declare any wooden or food items at customs. Keep a small amount of IDR for tips and last-minute expenses. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check in, settle into your boutique suite, enjoy a welcome drink and a complimentary foot soak ritual. Take a leisurely stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to decompress and soak in the lush green valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle sunset yoga session on the hotel's private terrace or rooftop overlooking the ridge. Followed by a relaxing dinner at the hotel's in-house restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport / during transfer
meals.dinner: In-house hotel restaurant — Balinese welcome dinner featuring rijsttafel (rice table) with local organic produce, paired with fresh coconut water or Balinese herbal drinks (jamu)

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. No activities before arrival. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 relaxed to adjust to the time zone. Warm weather (~25°C) — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hatha yoga class at a premium Ubud yoga studio (e.g., Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive) — book a private session for a personalized experience. Follow with a mindful walk along the Campuhan Ridge Walk at golden hour, watching the mist lift over the jungle valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in central Ubud for a curated guided tour. Afterward, explore Ubud's artisan market and Jalan Raya Ubud for premium handicrafts, textiles, and local art. Stop by a luxury gallery such as Neka Art Museum or ARMA Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Uluwatu (if arranged with private transfer). Dinner at a top Ubud fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — tropical fruit platters, Balinese black rice porridge, fresh-pressed juices, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Locavore NXT (Ubud) — plant-forward, locally sourced tasting menu in a chic setting
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique — award-winning fine dining with French-Balinese fusion cuisine; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Yoga Barn is approximately 15 minutes from Campuhan Ridge by private driver. Book Mozaic well in advance. Kecak dance at Pura Dalem starts around 19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Private Balinese Healing & Wellness Morning: Begin with a 90-minute traditional Balinese massage and flower bath at a luxury spa (e.g., COMO Shambhala Estate or Komaneka Spa). Follow with a private pranayama and meditation session with a local spiritual guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Ubud's royal heritage — visit Puri Saren Agung (Ubud Royal Palace), Saraswati Temple (Lotus Temple), and the historic Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) temple complex. Private driver and guide included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a cliffside bar or the hotel's terrace. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner experience arranged by the hotel with a bespoke menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast on sourdough, Balinese coffee (kopi Bali)
meals.lunch: Bridges Bali — elegant dining above the Campuhan River gorge, serving contemporary international cuisine
meals.dinner: Private in-villa or terrace candlelit dinner curated by the hotel chef — Balinese spiced seafood, organic salads, and local desserts

day_by_day.notes: COMO Shambhala Estate is a 5-minute drive from Campuhan Ridge. Goa Gajah is about 20 minutes away. Arrange private guide through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private sunrise yoga and breathwork session on the Campuhan Ridge with a certified instructor — one of Bali's most scenic outdoor yoga spots. Post-session, enjoy a healthy breakfast back at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Tegallalang Rice Terraces (UNESCO-listed) — private guided walk through the iconic stepped paddies. Visit a local subak (traditional irrigation cooperative). Continue to Tirta Empul Holy Spring Temple for a purification ritual (melukat) — a deeply spiritual Balinese experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Relaxing evening at the hotel's spa with a body scrub and aromatherapy treatment. Light, nourishing dinner at a wellness-focused restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga hotel breakfast — açaí bowls, granola with local honey, tropical fruits, herbal teas
meals.lunch: Sari Organik — farm-to-table restaurant set amid Tegallalang rice fields; organic Balinese dishes with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Clear Café Ubud — organic, wholesome menu with raw, vegan, and Balinese options; candlelit garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Tegallalang is approximately 20 minutes north of Ubud. Tirta Empul requires a sarong (provided at entrance). Best to visit Tirta Empul mid-morning to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private Balinese cooking class at a luxury culinary studio (e.g., Casa Luna Cooking School or Paon Bali) — learn to prepare traditional Balinese dishes using fresh market ingredients. Begin with an optional early morning visit to the Ubud traditional market to source ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon at the hotel — use the pool, read, or enjoy a private sound healing session (singing bowls) arranged through the concierge. Optional: visit a local silver or batik artisan workshop for a hands-on luxury craft experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga nidra (guided deep relaxation) session at the hotel or a nearby studio. Dinner at one of Ubud's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Balinese congee, fresh papaya with lime, cold-pressed green juice, Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class — a full Balinese feast enjoyed together with the instructor
meals.dinner: Room4Dessert — avant-garde dessert tasting experience by Chef Will Goldfarb (James Beard nominee); book well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically run 09:00–13:00 including market visit. Room4Dessert is a unique experience — dessert-only tasting menu. Reserve at least 2 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Mount Batur volcano region — depart early for a scenic drive to Kintamani. Enjoy a private guided walk around the Batur caldera rim with views of the volcano and Lake Batur. (Note: full summit hike optional but requires very early 03:00 start — recommend caldera rim walk for a luxury-paced experience.)
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the natural hot springs at Toya Devasya or Batur Natural Hot Spring — soak in geothermal mineral pools overlooking the volcano and lake. Private cabana and butler service available. Return to Ubud by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle restorative yoga session back at the hotel. Quiet, elegant dinner in Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast packed as a picnic or light breakfast before departure — banana bread, fruit, thermos of Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Panoramic lunch at Lakeview Restaurant, Kintamani — buffet or à la carte with sweeping volcano and lake views
meals.dinner: Hujan Locale — modern Indonesian fine dining in a beautifully restored Ubud heritage building

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 07:30 for Kintamani (approx. 1.5 hrs). Hot springs are best enjoyed mid-morning before crowds. Bring swimwear and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to the south — Seminyak/Uluwatu beach region (approx. 2 hrs). Check into a luxury beach villa or day-use suite (e.g., The Layar Private Villas, Seminyak, or Alila Villas Uluwatu). Morning beach yoga session on a private stretch of Seminyak Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a premium beach club — Ku De Ta, Potato Head Beach Club, or Finns Beach Club — with a private daybed, butler service, and ocean views. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy curated cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Iconic Uluwatu Sunset: Private transfer to Pura Luhur Uluwatu cliff temple for the legendary sunset Kecak fire dance (starts ~18:00). Dinner at a clifftop restaurant overlooking the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Ubud before departure — full spread of tropical fruits, eggs, pastries
meals.lunch: Potato Head Beach Club — vibrant beach dining with fresh seafood, salads, and craft cocktails
meals.dinner: Sundara at Four Seasons Jimbaran — beachfront fine dining with grilled seafood and contemporary cuisine; sunset views over Jimbaran Bay

day_by_day.notes: This is a beach day excursion from Ubud or a transition day if preferred. Uluwatu temple requires a sarong. Kecak dance tickets should be booked in advance. Return to Ubud hotel late evening or stay overnight at beach destination.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud (if day trip yesterday) or morning at leisure. Indulge in a luxurious spa morning at COMO Shambhala Estate — choose from Ayurvedic treatments, deep tissue massage, or a signature COMO Shambhala Journey (multi-treatment wellness ritual).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to East Ubud's hidden temples and villages — explore Pura Kehen (a stunning multi-tiered Hindu temple) in Bangli and the royal village of Penglipuran (one of Bali's cleanest and most traditional villages). Private driver and cultural guide included.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening in Ubud — attend a Legong or Barong dance performance at Ubud Palace (held most evenings). Dinner at a restaurant with live traditional Balinese music.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — nasi goreng (Balinese fried rice), tropical smoothie, fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — legendary Ubud institution serving the finest suckling pig (babi guling); a must-try cultural dining experience
meals.dinner: Alaya Resort Ubud Restaurant — sophisticated garden dining with panoramic Ubud views and refined Indonesian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: COMO Shambhala treatments should be booked 2–3 days in advance. Pura Kehen is about 45 minutes from Ubud. Penglipuran village has a small entrance fee. Ubud Palace performances start at 19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and meditation at a serene outdoor platform overlooking the Campuhan River valley. Follow with a guided Balinese spiritual walk — visit a local priest (pemangku) for a traditional blessing ceremony (optional but deeply meaningful).
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury day trip to Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples, perched on a dramatic offshore rock. Private guided tour with cultural context. Explore the surrounding coastal cliffs and rice paddies. Visit Pura Taman Ayun (Mengwi Royal Temple) en route.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar near Tanah Lot or return to Ubud for a relaxing evening. Indulgent dinner at a top-tier Ubud restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — post-yoga wellness spread: chia pudding, dragon fruit bowls, herbal infusions
meals.lunch: The Lumbung at Tanah Lot area — Balinese cuisine with rice terrace views
meals.dinner: Locavore — one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; innovative tasting menu celebrating Indonesian ingredients (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited late afternoon for sunset views (approx. 1.5 hrs from Ubud). Locavore is extremely popular — book 2–4 weeks in advance. Sarong required at temples.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury beach day excursion to Nusa Dua — depart by 08:00 with private driver. Arrive at a 5-star beach resort (e.g., The St. Regis Bali or Mulia Resort) for a day-use package including pool, beach access, and butler service. Morning swim and sunbathing on the calm, clear waters of Nusa Dua.
day_by_day.afternoon: Watersport experience: private snorkeling trip to the coral reefs of Nusa Dua, or a luxury sunset sailing charter along the Bali coast. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking in the calm lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sailing cocktail hour on the private charter. Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Nusa Dua or Jimbaran before returning to Ubud.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — light and energizing: fruit, yogurt, granola, Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: The Beach Club at Mulia Resort, Nusa Dua — premium beach dining with fresh seafood, sushi, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Merah Putih, Seminyak — stunning architectural space with refined Indonesian cuisine from across the archipelago

day_by_day.notes: Day-use packages at St. Regis or Mulia should be arranged 1–2 days ahead. Sailing charters depart from Benoa Harbor. Return to Ubud by 21:00. Nusa Dua waters are ideal for snorkeling — visibility excellent in July.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning dedicated to wellness and yoga — attend an advanced Vinyasa or Yin yoga masterclass at Yoga Barn (Ubud's premier yoga center). Follow with a private consultation with an Ayurvedic practitioner or nutritionist at the hotel or COMO Shambhala Estate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's creative arts scene — visit the Blanco Renaissance Museum (home of the eccentric Spanish-Balinese artist Antonio Blanco), then browse the galleries along Monkey Forest Road. Commission a custom piece from a local Balinese artist. Visit a traditional Balinese healer (balian) for an optional traditional healing consultation (arrange through concierge).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-finale dinner — celebrate the penultimate evening with a luxury multi-course dinner at Ubud's finest. Enjoy live gamelan music and a nightcap at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full luxury spread: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, açaí bowls, fresh juices
meals.lunch: Kebun Bistro — charming garden restaurant in Ubud with fresh, seasonal European-Balinese fusion dishes
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique (second visit or alternative: Apéritif Restaurant) — Apéritif offers a 7-course colonial-era inspired tasting menu in a spectacular Art Deco setting

day_by_day.notes: Yoga Barn class schedule varies — check and book online. Blanco Museum has a small entrance fee. Balian (traditional healer) sessions are deeply personal — discuss with concierge for trusted recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the Campuhan Ridge Walk — a peaceful, reflective practice to honor the journey. Private guided walk through the ridge as the morning mist clears over the jungle. Visit the historic Pura Gunung Lebah temple at the base of the ridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping and souvenir curation in Ubud — visit premium boutiques for handcrafted jewelry (e.g., Kou Cuisine & Boutique), hand-dyed ikat textiles, and artisan home goods. Optional: private batik or silver jewelry making workshop. Last spa treatment — choose a signature Balinese boreh (herbal body wrap) or a traditional Javanese lulur scrub.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the finest dining experience of the trip. Dress elegantly for a celebratory meal at Ubud's most prestigious restaurant. Toast to an extraordinary Bali journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full luxury spread to fuel the last full day: nasi goreng, tropical fruit, pastries, Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Swept Away at COMO Shambhala Estate — health-focused gourmet cuisine in a stunning open-air jungle setting beside the Wos River
meals.dinner: Apéritif Restaurant, Ubud — 7-course or 9-course tasting menu with wine pairing; one of Bali's most celebrated fine-dining experiences in a grand colonial villa

day_by_day.notes: Pura Gunung Lebah is a short walk from the hotel at the bottom of the ridge — serene and rarely crowded. Book Apéritif well in advance. This is the last full day — arrange any packing and confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — gentle sunrise meditation or yoga on the hotel terrace. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast. Take a final walk along the Campuhan Ridge to say goodbye to the lush Ubud landscape. Check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow 2–2.5 hours for the journey). Depending on flight time, enjoy a final stop at a premium café or spa lounge near the airport (e.g., Bali Collection, Nusa Dua, or airport lounge access). Depart Bali.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days — beaches, yoga, temples, and the soul of Bali.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a leisurely, indulgent spread: fresh tropical fruits, Balinese black rice pudding, eggs to order, farewell jamu herbal drink
meals.lunch: Airport or en-route — Nusa Dua's The Laguna Resort café for a light farewell lunch if time permits, or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with hotel (standard is 12:00; request late checkout if needed). Private airport transfer should be arranged the night before. Keep one piece of luggage accessible for any last-minute purchases. Tip hotel staff generously — a Balinese tradition of gratitude.
